what_it_does: Quantum computers use physical particles called qubits to do computation, and running a quantum program usually requires one qubit per logical role — a wasteful constraint. This paper looks at 'qubit reuse': taking a qubit that finished its job early, resetting it on the fly (via a mid-circuit measurement), and assigning it a new role, so fewer physical qubits are needed overall. Finding the best reuse schedule is a notoriously hard combinatorial search (in the same family as problems like the travelling-salesman puzzle), and prior methods either blow up in search time or produce non-optimal results. QR-Map solves this by re-expressing the circuit's dependencies as a structured map — think of it like aligning two sequences of two-qubit operations into a grid so that dependency conflicts become visually obvious and can be detected in a predictable, non-random way. The approach is guaranteed to find valid reuse opportunities in time that grows polynomially (not exponentially) with circuit size, and it jointly manages both depth (how many steps the circuit takes) and crosstalk (unwanted interference between nearby qubits).
